framework.summary: Each frontier developer must develop, publish and follow a Model Safety Plan with a risk assessment, mitigation measures and a responsible corporate officer for each model it creates or substantially modifies.
framework.quote: Each developer shall develop, publish, and follow a safety plan (referred to in this section as the ``Model Safety Plan'') for each artificial intelligence system or model

transparency_report.summary: Developers must publish their Model Safety Plan, which includes a capabilities or risk assessment for the model.
transparency_report.quote: Each developer shall develop, publish, and follow a safety plan

incident_reporting.summary: Frontier developers and critical-infrastructure operators using AI must report confirmed AI safety or security incidents within 30 days of confirmation.
incident_reporting.quote: shall report any confirmed artificial intelligence safety incident or artificial intelligence security incident within 30 days of confirmation of such incident

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: An incident posing an imminent threat to national security, critical infrastructure or public safety must be reported within 72 hours.
imminent_risk_reporting.quote: within 72 hours if such incident poses an imminent threat to national security, critical infrastructure, or public safety

third_party_audit.summary: Developers must give a federal Safety Board access to a frontier model, including weights, 45 days before release; this is government evaluation, not an independent audit.
third_party_audit.quote: Not later than 45 calendar days before a developer introduces into interstate or foreign commerce a frontier artificial intelligence model, the developer shall make available to the Board access to the frontier artificial intelligence model

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no whistleblower protections.

registration.summary: Each Model Safety Plan must be filed with the Commerce Secretary; there is no license or approval to develop or deploy.
registration.quote: Each Model Safety Plan shall be submitted to the Secretary in the form and manner determined by the Secretary.

shutdown.summary: Board standards, still to be written, must cover prompt termination of risky AI evaluations; no kill switch for deployed models.

compute_threshold.summary: Coverage is by capability for frontier models, with no compute figure.

revenue_threshold.summary: The bill defines coverage by no revenue, spending or user figure.

harm_threshold.summary: The bill sets no death, injury or damages threshold; incidents are defined as events that materially increase risk.

penalties.summary: A developer that violates a Board standard faces a civil penalty up to $250,000 per violation, each day a separate violation; the Commerce Secretary enforces and the Attorney General may sue.
penalties.quote: A developer that violates subsection (c) shall be liable to the United States for a civil penalty of not more than $250,000 for each violation.

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; deadlines run from enactment (Board within 30 days).

notes: Penalties in Sec. 3(d) attach only to violating adopted Board standards (Sec. 3(c)); no penalty is stated for Sec. 4 safety plan or Sec. 5 incident reporting duties. Standards (Sec. 3(a)(6)) are still to be written. Incident database submissions in Sec. 5(a)(1) are voluntary, Sec. 5(a)(3) mandatory.
